question: A 14-month-old boy was diagnosed with Hemophilus influenza meningitis. The initialtreatment plan was to start on ampicillin but later was shifted to ceftriaxone. What could bethe probable reason?

options.a: Hemophilus alters penicillin binding protein sites, hence resistant to ampicillin
options.b: Easier to administer IV ceftriaxone than IV ampicillin
options.c: Cotrimoxazole is the drug of choice, but patient is allergic to sulfa drugs
options.d: Hemophilus produces beta lactamase, hence resistant to ampicillin

explanation: The probable reason why the drug to be administered was changed from ampicillin to ceftriaxoneis because Hemophilus produces beta-lactamase and hence, is resistant to ampicillin. A considerable percentage of isolates of Hemophilus influenzae produce beta-lactamase,rendering them resistant to ampicillin, a beta-lactam antibiotic. However, these strains are stillsensitive to second and third-generation cephalosporins. In H. influenzae, the resistance to ampicillin and other β-lactam antibiotics is generally due to theproduction of a β-lactamase. In the case of β-lactamase-negative ampicillin-resistant strains,resistance is due to the presence of altered penicillin-binding proteins. Ceftriaxone is a third-generation cephalosporin that is effective against HemophilusInfluenzae and considerably resistant to beta-lactamase. It has a very long half-life which permitsonce-daily dosing of the drug. Because of the efficacy of third-generation cephalosporins in thetherapy of meningitis caused by Hemophilus Influenzae type b, ceftriaxone administered at therate of 50 mg/kg/dose given 12th hourly should be a part of the initial empirical therapy. Vancomycin combined with a third-generation cephalosporin like ceftriaxone is the recommendedempirical antibiotic regimen in a suspected case of meningitis, beyond the neonatal period.
subject: Pharmacology

question: A patient who is a known case of cirrhosis of the liver presents with abdominal distension andswelling of the lower limbs. The preferred diuretic for this patient would be
explanation: The preferred diuretic for this patient with cirrhosis presenting with abdominal distension andlower limb swelling is eplerenone. Eplerenone is a mineralocorticoid receptor/aldosterone antagonist. High doses ofmineralocorticoid receptor/aldosterone antagonists decrease total body sodium in cirrhoticpatients with ascites by natriuresis. 1138 Patients with liver cirrhosis have a decreased effective arterial blood volume because of splanchnicvasodilatation. This stimulates the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system and results inhyperaldosteronism. This causes increased sodium and water retention and leads to thedevelopment of ascites. This also contributes to resistance to loop diuretics. Normally, aldosterone (AL) enters the cells of the late distal tubule and collecting ducts bydiffusion and binds to a specific mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) in the cytoplasm. This AL-MRcomplex mediates Na+ reabsorption, which drives the secretion of K+ and H+into the tubules. Eplerenone competitively blocks this MR, preventing it from binding with aldosterone. The neteffect is sodium diuresis and potassium retention. It is a potassium-sparing diuretic. Othermineralocorticoid receptor antagonists include spironolactone, canrenone, potassium canrenoate. Some clinical uses of MR antagonists are - • Hypertension due to primary hyperaldosteronism • Edema associated with liver cirrhosis, congestive cardiac failure, chronic kidney disease • They may reduce mortality in patients with myocardial infarction Hyperkalemia is the major side effect of MR antagonists, the risk being greater in patients withrenal disease or those already taking ACE inhibitors. Other important side effects aregynecomastia and decreased libido due to the anti-androgenic effect of spironolactone buteplerenone does not cause gynecomastia and decreased libido. Other options : Option A- Triamterene directly inhibits renal epithelial sodium channels (ENaC) in the late distaltubule and collecting duct. It is a potassium-sparing diuretic and is generally used along withother diuretics in the treatment of hypertension and edema. Triamterene is metabolized in theliver, hence triamterene toxicity may be enhanced in patients with hepatic disease. It is used inthe management of Liddle syndrome. Option C- Chlorthalidone is a thiazide-like diuretic. It inhibits Na+-Cl- symporter in the earlydistal tubule and increases the excretion of sodium and chloride. Thiazide diuretics may be usedfor the treatment of hypertension, heart failure, nephrolithiasis due to idiopathic hypercalciuria,and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. Option D- Furosemide is a loop diuretic. It acts by inhibiting the Na+-K+-2Cl- symporter in thethick ascending limb of the loop of Henle resulting in increased excretion of sodium and chloride.It also has mild carbonic anhydrase inhibitory activity and also increases urinary excretion ofbicarbonate and phosphate. Cirrhotic patients are often resistant to loop diuretics dueto decreased secretion of the drug into tubular fluid and high aldosterone levels. Furosemide maybe given along with eplerenone, but the best answer here is eplerenone since aldosteroneantagonists are the main therapy for cirrhotic edema.
subject: Pharmacology

question: Which of the following is the most effective drug in smoking cessation?
explanation: Varenicline is the most effective drug in smoking cessation. Nicotine is the principal constituent of tobacco responsible for its addictive behaviour. One of thenewest agents introduced to aid in smoking cessation is varenicline. 1139 Varenicline works by blocking the effects of nicotine on the brain. It blocks α-4, β-2 nicotinicacetylcholine receptor subtypes and varenicline inhibits dopaminergic activation produced bysmoking through their partial agonism, and decreases the craving and withdrawal syndrome thatoccurs with cessation attempts. It prevents nicotine stimulation of the mesolimbic dopaminesystem associated with nicotine addiction, thus helping to occlude the "rewarding" effect ofsmoking. Varenicline is prescribed only to patients 18 years or older. Varenicline is taken orally and thedose taken is 0.5 mg once daily on days 1 to 3, increased to 0.5 mg twice daily on days 4 through 7and 1 mg twice daily after day 8 for 11 weeks. Therapy should start one week before the target quitdate. It can be continued for another 12 weeks (1 mg BD) to maintain abstinence. The adverse effects include nausea, which can be mitigated by starting at lower doses andgradually increasing the dose. Other symptoms include disturbed sleep, sleepwalking, agitation,drowsiness, and constipation and may also increase the risk of pancreatitis. Varenicline has alsobeen implicated in specific skin syndromes such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome, erythemamultiforme, and photosensitivity. Varenicline can cause renal failure and kidney stones, thus renalfunction must be monitored. The FDA has issued a warning about mood and behavioral changes associated with its use, andthere is some evidence of increased cardiovascular risk. Other options: Option B: Buspirone sustained release is a partial agonist at 5HT receptors but affinity for D2receptors may also be present. Its effects are slow onset, over a couple of weeks and is used in themanagement of generalised anxiety states. Option C: Nicotine gum has nicotine which is an agonist at Nn type nicotinic cholinergic receptorsand is also advised for smoking cessation along with psychotherapy. However, varenicline wasmore effective when compared with singleIproduct nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) and wassimilarly effective compared with combination NRT. Option D: Rimonabant is an inverse agonist at cannabinoid receptor CB1 which decreasesneurotransmitter release at GABAergic and glutamatergic synapses; its usage for smokingcessation and treat obesity was stopped after serious side effects notably severe depression andincreased risk of suicide. However, it continues to be used off-label for smoking cessation.
subject: Pharmacology

question: A patient who was on warfarin therapy for atrial fibrillation is prescribed a cephalosporinantibiotic for the treatment of a lower respiratory tract infection. He reports back to thehospital after having developed hemarthrosis. Which of the following cephalosporins is likelyto have caused this?
explanation: The cephalosporin antibiotic most likely to have caused hemarthrosis in this patient on warfarintherapy is cefoperazone. Cephalosporins containing a methylthiotetrazole (NMTT) group can prolong the prothrombintime. This results in clinically significant bleeding in patients already on anticoagulant therapy orhaving vitamin K deficiency. This is because NMTT cephalosporins inhibit the enzyme vitamin K epoxide reductase in the liver,which is the key enzyme for vitamin K-dependent carboxylation, a posttranslational modificationthat is essential for the biological functions of coagulation factors. 1140 NMTT group containing cephalosporins include latamoxef, cefmenoxime, cefoperazone, cefotetan,cefamandole. Vitamin K epoxide reductase is also the target of anticoagulants like warfarin. Oral administrationof vitamin K can prevent this problem.
subject: Pharmacology

question: Which of the following is a novel anti-depressant?
explanation: Vilazodone is the novel antidepressant. The antidepressant effect of vilazodone is due to its enhancement of serotonergic activity in theCNS through selective inhibition of serotonin reuptake. It binds with high affinity to the serotoninreuptake site but not to the norepinephrine or dopamine reuptake site. As a result, vilazodonepotently and selectively inhibits the reuptake of serotonin. Vilazodone is also a partial agonist at serotonergic 5-HT1A receptors; the result of this activity onserotonergic transmission also plays a role in its antidepressant effect. Thus it offers a novel combination of selective serotonin reuptake inhibition (SSRI) andserotonergic (5-HT1A) receptor partial agonist activity. Because of these characteristics,vilazodone has been termed a serotonin partial agonist–reuptake inhibitor (SPARI). Vilazodone is never combined with a monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitor or given within 14 daysof discontinuing or initiating MAO inhibitor therapy due to the serious risk of serotonin toxicity. Other options: Option A: Lurasidone is a second-generation antipsychotic that is a 5-HT2A and D2 receptorantagonist. it is used in the treatment of schizophrenia and bipolar depression (as monotherapy oras an adjunct). Option C: Asenapine is a second-generation antipsychotic which is also a 5-HT2A and D2 receptorantagonist, used in the management of schizophrenia and acute mania. Option D: Blonanserin is a second-generation antipsychotic, which acts as an antagonist at D2,D3, and 5-HT2A receptors. Blonanserin has a low affinity for 5-HT2C, adrenergic α1, histamineH1, and muscarinic M1 receptors, but displays a relatively high affinity for 5-HT6 receptors. It isused in the management of schizophrenia.
subject: Pharmacology

question: A 57-year-old man was brought to the hospital with complaints of dizziness andbreathlessness. During his physical examination, you notice the following discolouration overhis face. He is presently being treated with amiodarone, metoprolol, verapamil, lisinopril, andamlodipine. Which of the following drugs is most likely responsible?
explanation: The image shows grey-blue discoloration over this patient's face and the drug responsible for thisis amiodarone. Long-term treatment with amiodarone is responsible for skin pigmentation. Elderly men are at anincreased risk of developing this. Ultraviolet light reacts with amiodarone and its metabolites to cause local vasodilatation. Thisincreases the diffusion of amiodarone and its metabolites, resulting in their deposition in thetissues, causing pigmentation. Therefore, it is usually seen in sun-exposed areas. 1141 Cessation of amiodarone, avoiding exposure to sunlight using sunscreen cream is recommended. Amiodarone is an iodine-containing compound that is structurally related to thyroid hormone. Itis a class III antiarrhythmic drug, which increases the duration of an action potential by blockingpotassium channels. It thereby increases the time taken for repolarization. It also prolongs therefractory period and suppresses abnormal automaticity. It also has weak calcium channelblocking, sodium channel blocking, and adrenergic blocking actions. It is used to maintain normal sinus rhythm during atrial fibrillation and prevent recurrentventricular tachycardia. Adverse effects of amiodarone: • Prolonged usage of amiodarone causes interstitial lung disease. • Heart blocks, bradycardia and QT prolongation • Hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism • Corneal micro-deposits and vortex keratopathy, optic neuropathy Drug interactions of amiodarone • Causes digoxin toxicity by decreasing its renal clearance. • Increases concentration of quinidine and procainamide • Potentiates the anticoagulant effect of warfarin when given simultaneously
subject: Pharmacology

question: Which of the following is a centrally acting opioid antitussive?
explanation: Levopropoxyphene is a centrally acting opioid antitussive. Levopropoxyphene is an opioid derivative that is a strong and partial µ receptor agonist that helpsto reduce the cough reflex and therefore, is used in the management of acute debilitating cough.The usual antitussive dose is 50–100 mg every 4 hours. It has no analgesic activity. However, it isknown to cause some sedation. Other options: Option A: Ambroxol is derived from bromhexine. It is a mucoactive agent that helps alter theviscoelastic properties of mucus and increase mucociliary clearance, thereby providing relief inproductive cough. It is commonly available as intramuscular or intravenous, lozenges, syrups, ortablets. Option B: Diphenoxylate is an opioid agonist that is structurally similar to meperidine. It is usedin the treatment of acute, chronic, and traveler's diarrhea. Upon administration, it undergoesde-esterification to difenoxin, which is its active metabolite. Its side effects include constipation,toxic megacolon, paralytic ileus and can give rise to CNS depression in children. Option D: Levorphanol is a synthetic opioid that is also a 5HT/Norepinephrine reuptake inhibitorand an NMDA receptor antagonist which is chiefly used in the management of moderate to severepain and has a relatively rapid onset of action. Its side effects include delirium and hallucinations. 1142
subject: Pharmacology

question: The anti-epileptic drugs which can also be used for the treatment of neuropathic pain are
explanation: The anti-epileptic drugs which can also be used for neuropathic pain are 1, 2, and 4 which arepregabalin, carbamazepine and gabapentin respectively. Pregabalin is an anti-epileptic drug that acts by binding to α2δ, a protein that is a subunit ofvoltage-gated calcium channels and causes a decrease in glutamate release at excitatory synapses.It is used in the management of neuropathic pain associated with diabetic peripheral neuropathy,spinal cord injury or postherpetic neuralgia. Gabapentin is an anti-epileptic drug that, like pregabalin, acts by binding to α2δ protein. It is usedin the management of neuropathic pain due to postherpetic neuralgia in adults. The binding of gabapentin and pregabalin, also called "gabapentinoids" due to their structuralsimilarity to GABA, to calcium channel subunit a2δ protein, is considered to mediate theanti-convulsant effects of gabapentin and pregabalin. They are used in focal onset seizures with orwithout progression to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures when used in addition to other anti-epilepticdrugs. Carbamazepine is an iminostilbine derivative. It blocks voltage-activated sodiumchannels, slowing their rate of recovery and limiting the repetitive firing of action potentials. It isused in the treatment of: • Generalized, focal-to-bilateral and idiopathic tonic-clonic seizures • Focal seizures • Neuropathic pain associated with trigeminal and glossopharyngeal neuralgias. Lamotrigine is an anti-folate agent whose mechanism of action is similar to that of carbamazepinei.e. it delays the recovery from inactivation of recombinant sodium channels. It also inhibits therelease of glutamate by acting directly on the sodium channels. Therefore, when usedconcurrently with carbamazepine, is associated with toxicity in some patients due to increase in10,11- epoxide of carbamazepine. It is useful in the management of: • Focal and secondarily generalized tonic-clonic seizures in adults • Lennox-Gastaut syndrome - a childhood disorder characterized by multiple type seizures, mentalretardation, and refractoriness to anti-seizure medication.
subject: Pharmacology

question: A breast cancer patient post-chemotherapy developed a low-grade fever with anemia andleukocytopenia (<4000/cm3; DNC: 30). Which of the following antibiotics will not be usedin the empirical management of this patient?
explanation: Linezolid cannot be used in this patient as bone Synopsis suppression is a side effect of this drugand hence it can worsen the post-chemotherapy bone Synopsis suppression in this patient. Linezolid can cause myelosuppression which can present as anemia, thrombocytopenia,leukopenia, and pancytopenia. It is commonly associated with thrombocytopenia and is seen 7-10days following administration. This is usually reversed on discontinuation of the drug. Other adverse effects of linezolid: • It inhibits mitochondrial protein synthesis and may lead to peripheral neuropathy, opticneuritis, and lactic acidosis in patients receiving the drug for longer durations. 1143 • It can cause serotonin syndrome when coadministered with adrenergic or serotonergic drugs likeSSRIs due to its nonspecific MAO inhibition. It is a protein synthesis inhibitor of the class oxazolidinones. It mainly acts against gram-positiveorganisms. It is approved for the treatment of the following conditions: • Skin and skin structure infections by staphylococcus(Both MRSA and MSSA) and streptococcus. • Community-acquired pneumonia due to streptococcus pneumoniae. • Nosocomial pneumonia due to staphylococcus aureus. Other options: Cefepime: It is a fourth-generation antipseudomonal cephalosporin. It is useful in enterobacterand pseudomonas infections that are resistant to other cephalosporins. Piperacillin-Tazobactam- It is a combination of piperacillin which is a ureidopenicillin andtazobactam which is a beta-lactamase inhibitor. It is useful in various infections includingnosocomial infections, intraabdominal infections, pneumonia, and UTI. It is highly effectiveagainst E Coli and Klebsiella. Meropenem: It belongs to the carbapenem group of beta-lactam antibiotics. They are more activeagainst gram-negative organisms. Coadministration of cilastatin is not required with this drug.(Cilastation should be coadministered with imipenem as imipenem is sensitive to renal peptidasedegradation) 1144
subject: Pharmacology

question: A female patient on oral contraceptive pills (OCP) was diagnosed to have tuberculosis andstarted on antitubercular therapy (ATT). She was advised to use an additional barrier methodof contraception. What is the reason for this advice?

options.d: Rifampicin induces OCP metabolism and cause failure

explanation: Rifampicin is a potent cytochrome P450 (CYP450) enzyme inducer. When given along with oralcontraceptive pills(OCP) it would induce the metabolism of OCPs leading to contraceptive failure.This is the reason for the patient being advised to use an additional method of contraception. Important enzyme inducers are: • Barbiturates • Phenytoin • Carbamazepine • Rifampicin • Cigarette smoking • Chronic alcoholism Important drugs that inhibit CYP450 isoenzyme are: • Macrolide antibiotics • Azole antifungals • Chloramphenicol • Omeprazole • Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) • HIV protease inhibitors • Cimetidine • Ciprofloxacin 1150 • Metronidazole
subject: Pharmacology

question: A 35-year-old chronic hypertensive woman visits the outpatient department forpre-conceptional counseling. Which of the following anti-hypertensives should shediscontinue?
explanation: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors should be discontinued in pregnancy as they cancause hypoplasia of organs, growth retardation, and fetal loss. ACE inhibitors cause reduced perfusion and oligohydramnios leading to fetal growth retardation,calvarium maldevelopment, hypoplasia of lungs and kidneys, and limb contractures. Antihypertensive drugs to be avoided in pregnancy: • ACE inhibitors and Angiotensin receptor blockers(ARB) - Can cause growth retardation and fetaldamage. • Diuretics - Can decrease uteroplacental perfusion • Nonselective beta-blockers • Sodium nitroprusside - It is contraindicated in eclampsia. Antihypertensive drugs that can be used in pregnancy: • Labetalol - Combined α + β blocker • Nifedipine - Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker. It is useful in preeclampsia but should bestopped before labor as they weaken the uterine contractions. • Methyldopa • Hydralazine Note: Thiazide diuretics like hydrochlorothiazide are considered to be safe in pregnancy and are usefulin the management of chronic hypertension in pregnant women.
subject: Pharmacology

question: A pregnant woman was prescribed indomethacin. Which of the following effects does thedrug have on the fetus?
explanation: Indomethacin can cause premature closure of ductus arteriosus if given to a pregnant woman. Indomethacin is approved for the closure of persistent ductus arteriosus in premature infants. Itis given intravenously. One of its limiting factors is the development of renal toxicity in neonates. Indomethacin is a nonselective COX inhibitor. It has anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antipyreticproperties. It can be used in the management of conditions like rheumatoid arthritis, goutyarthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, etc. But its use is limited due to the high rate ofintolerance and availability of safer agents. Adverse effects: Diarrhea with ulcerative bowel lesions, acute pancreatitis, and hepatitis are seen.Frontal headache is the most frequent CNS effect. Dizziness, light-headedness, vertigo, andmental confusion can occur. Neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, and rarely aplastic anemia can alsooccur. 1151 Note: Prostaglandin analogs are indicated in the maintenance of patency of the ductus arteriosus.
subject: Pharmacology

question: Which of the following can be prescribed in case of an open angle glaucoma with bronchialasthma?
explanation: Latanoprost can be given in a case of open-angle glaucoma with bronchial asthma. Latanoprost is a PGF2α analog and it is not associated with systemic side effects likebronchospasm and hence can be given for asthmatic patients. Prostaglandin analogs are the firstchoice drugs for open-angle glaucoma. Mechanism of action: It reduces intraocular pressure by altering the ciliary muscle tension andimproving the outflow of the aqueous humor. Advantages of latanoprost: • Good efficacy • Once-daily application • Absence of systemic side effects Disadvantage: High cost Adverse effects: • Blurring of vision • Iris pigmentation • Thickening and darkening of eyelashes • Macular edema can occur especially in aphakic patients. Other options: Option A- Timolol is a non-selective beta-blocker used topically in glaucoma. It is associated withsystemic effects by absorption through the nasolacrimal duct and can cause life-threateningbronchospasm in asthmatics and COPD patients. Hence they are not given in in this case. Option B- Gemeprost is a PGE1 analog used for the termination of early pregnancy. Option D- Mannitol infusion is given for acute congestive glaucoma and not for open-angleglaucoma. It causes decongestion of the eye by its osmotic action.
subject: Pharmacology

question: As a medical practitioner in India, how will you prescribe alprazolam to a patient?

options.a: 1 mg OD before bedtime for 7 days
options.d: 0.5 mg daily before bedtime for 7 days

explanation: The correct method of prescribing alprazolam is 0.5mg daily before bedtime for 7 days. The drugs are prescribed in generic names legibly and preferably in capital letters. Theprescription should have details to identify the patient and medication that needs to be dispensedand the therapeutic purpose. The use of abbreviations, especially Latin is discouraged. The dosageshould be written in metric measure. 1152 Guidelines for drug prescription: The parts of an ideal prescription are as follows. • Date • Name and address of the doctor • Superscription(Rx symbol) • Information about the patient • Name and dose of the drug prescribed(Inscription) • Dispencing directions to the pharmacist(Subscription) • Instructions for the patient • Signature of the doctor
subject: Pharmacology

question: A patient started on antihypertensive presented with the following picture. Which of thefollowing drugs is the most likely cause?
explanation: The image shows edema over the lips and face and its occurrence following intake of anantihypertensive is suggestive of drug-induced angioedema. Lisinopril being an ACE inhibitor ismost likely to be responsible for this condition. Angioedema with ACE inhibitors: In very few patients(0.1%-0.5%), ACE inhibitors cause rapid swelling in the nose, throat, mouth,glottis, larynx, lips, or tongue. Once the drug is stopped symptoms improve drastically over hours.Angioedema of the intestine can occur very rarely. ACE inhibitor-associated angioedema is a class effect, and patients who develop this adverse eventshould not be prescribed any other drugs within the ACE inhibitor class. Other adverse effects of ACE inhibitors: Hypotension - A sudden fall in blood pressure can occur following the first dose of ACE inhibitors. Cough - It can produce a bothersome dry cough due to the accumulation of bradykinin, substanceP, or prostaglandins in the lungs. The cough usually disappears within 4 days of the stoppage ofthe drug. Hyperkalemia due to K+ retention can occur. Acute renal failure can occur with ACE inhibitors in patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis,stenosis of the artery to a single remaining kidney, heart failure, or volume depletion dueto diarrhea or diuretics. It should be discontinued in pregnant women as it can cause developmental defects. It can also cause maculopapular skin rash in some cases. Other options: Option B: Nifedipine is a calcium channel blocker. Common adverse effects include headache,flushing, and dizziness. Peripheral edema may rarely occur. 1153 Option C: Atenolol is a beta 1 selective antagonist. Bradycardia, fatigue, cold extremities arecommon adverse effects. CNS side effects like nightmares and depression are less frequent withatenolol than other beta-blockers. Option D: Clonidine is an alpha-2 adrenergic agonist. The main adverse effects of clonidine aredry mouth and sedation. Bradycardia and sexual dysfunction are other effects.
subject: Pharmacology

question: A patient on aspirin presented with occult blood in the stool. This is due to inhibition of____by aspirin
explanation: Aspirin causes inhibition of cyclooxygenase-1(COX-1) which would inhibit the formation ofthromboxane A2. Thromboxane A2 is an inducer of platelet aggregation and is a potentvasoconstrictor. Hence inhibition of its formation is responsible for the bleeding complications ofaspirin. Aspirin is a noncompetitive, irreversible inhibitor of the cyclooxygenase(COX) enzyme. It is anonselective COX inhibitor and inhibits both COX-1 and COX-2. Uses of aspirin: • Analgesic and antipyretic uses. • Acute rheumatic fever • Rheumatoid arthritis • Post myocardial infarction and stroke due to its antiplatelet action. • Prevention of preeclampsia Adverse effects: Nausea, vomiting, epigastric discomfort, and increased occult blood in stools are seen withanalgesic doses(0.5-2g/day). Antiinflammatory doses(3-5g/day) can produce salicylismcharacterized by dizziness, tinnitus, vertigo, hyperventilation, reversible loss of hearing andvision, etc. It can cause elevation of liver enzymes and hepatic damage. Hypersensitivity reactionsare also seen. Reye's syndrome is a rare condition that can occur when salicylates like aspirin are given inchildren having viral infections like influenza.
subject: Pharmacology

question: A 60-year-old postmenopausal female patient with a previous history of Colle's fracture camewith complaints of lower backache. On evaluation, her T score was -2.5. Which of thefollowing statements are false about the management of her condition?

options.a: Teriparatide should be started before supplementing with bisphosphonates
options.b: Bisphosphonates are not given for more than a year
options.c: Calcium requirement is 1200 mg per day
options.d: Oral vitamin D3 is given along with oral calcium

explanation: Bisphosphonates are given for periods of more than one year (Option B is false). In this case, asthe patient is having a history of osteoporotic fracture, teriparatide can be given beforebisphosphonates. Pharmacologic management of osteoporosis: Bisphosphonates: These are pyrophosphate analogs that act by directly inhibiting bone resorption.The antiresorptive action is mainly due to its direct inhibitory effect on osteoclasts. Itcauses osteoclast apoptosis as well as the prevention of hydroxyapatite dissolution. Long-termbisphosphonates therapy is given for durations of 3-5 years, depending on the fracture risk of the 1154 patient. Since they are associated with osteonecrosis of the jaw and atypical femur fractures, adrug holiday may be advised after long-term management. Teriparatide is a recombinant PTH analog that has an anabolic effect on bone homeostasisby increasing osteoblastic activity. It increases bone mineral density and decreases the risk offractures in postmenopausal women. Indications of teriparatide therapy include the history ofosteoporotic fracture, multiple risk factors for fracture, intolerance, or failure of previousosteoporosis therapy. It is only approved for 2 years of use. Clinical trials that used teriparatideprior to bisphosphonate have been proven effective. Denosumab is a human monoclonal antibody with a mechanism of action similar to that ofosteoprotegerin (OPG). It binds to RANK Ligand (RANKL), thereby inhibiting its binding to theRANK receptor of the surface of osteoclasts. This prevents RANK receptor activation andsubsequent bone resorption. Selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs) - Estrogen has a protective effect that preventsaccelerated bone loss. This is carried out by reducing the bone resorption effects of parathyroidhormone (PTH). Keeping in line with these effects, osteoporosis prevention in postmenopausalwomen has been attributed to the use of SERMs such as raloxifene. It acts as an estrogen agoniston the bone and liver. Calcium and Vitamin D supplementation: Calcium supplementation in the elderly suppressesbone turnover and improves bone mineral density. 1200mg of calcium is daily required in adultsof more than 50 years of age. Vitamin D supplementation with 400-800IU/day improvesintestinal calcium absorption, suppresses bone remodeling, and improves bone mineral density.
subject: Pharmacology

question: A patient presented with a history of multiple episodes of vomiting. He was given anintravenous drug, and later, he developed abnormal movements. Which of the following canbe used to treat him?
explanation: Benzhexol should be used in the management of this patient. The development of abnormalmovements following an anti-emetic injection suggests that the antiemetic used in this case isprobably metoclopramide. Metoclopramide is a dopamine receptor antagonist used as a prokinetic and anti-emetic agent. Itcan produce extrapyramidal side effects and dystonia is seen acutely following intravenousinjections. Anticholinergics like benzhexol (trihexyphenidyl) are used in the management of theseside effects. Benzhexol is a centrally-acting anticholinergic agent. It acts by restoring thecholinergic balance in the striatal interneurons. Extrapyramidal side effects of metoclopramide are commonly seen in children and young adultswith higher doses. Acute dystonia occurs after intravenous administration, whileparkinsonian-like symptoms develop weeks after therapy. It is managed with the discontinuationof metoclopramide and with anticholinergics or antihistaminics. Irreversible tardive dyskinesiacan occur with chronic treatment. Other adverse effects: It can cause galactorrhea by its dopamine antagonism. Methemoglobinemia can occur if used ininfants. Other options: 1155 Option A: Hyoscine (scopolamine): It is a muscarinic receptor antagonist used in the managementof motion sickness and vomiting. Option B: Cyproheptadine is an H1 receptor antagonist used in the management of variousallergy-related conditions like allergic rhinitis, anaphylaxis, urticaria, etc. Option C: Levodopa is the precursor of dopamine and it is given in combination with carbidopafor the management of parkinsonism.
subject: Pharmacology

question: What formula is the dosing rate of a drug based on?
explanation: The formula for drug dosing rate is clearance x plasma concentration. The equation for dose rate given here is based on steady-state concentration. When a drug is givenrepeatedly at short intervals it will accumulate in the body until the elimination of the drugmatches its input. So steady-state concentration is the plasma concentration at which the drugelimination and drug input balance each other. Steady-state concentration(Cpss) = Dose rate / Clearance From this equation dose rate for a target steady-state plasma concentration is calculated as Dose rate = Clearance(CL) x target plasma concentration(Cpss)
subject: Pharmacology

question: A patient on digoxin, potassium chloride, clarithromycin, atenolol, and triamterenedeveloped atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular rate. Serum digoxin levels were raised.Which of his medications is responsible for the same?
explanation: Elevated serum digoxin levels and the development of atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricularrate are suggestive of digoxin toxicity. Clarithromycin when given along with digoxin can causedigoxin toxicity. P-glycoprotein pumps play a major role in the elimination of digoxin. Drugs that inhibitP-glycoprotein can thereby decrease the elimination of digoxin and lead to digoxin toxicity.Macrolide antibiotics like clarithromycin and erythromycin are inhibitors of the P-glycoprotein.So clarithromycin when given along with digoxin can cause digoxin toxicity. Other drugs that inhibit P-glycoprotein are - Amiodarone, quinidine, verapamil, diltiazem,cyclosporine, itraconazole, propafenone, and flecainide. Digoxin is one of the cardiac glycosides which is derived from the digitalis plant and usedclinically. It inhibits Na+/K+ ATPase, a membrane-bound transporter to increase intracellular sodium. As aresult, there is less expulsion of calcium from the cell by sodium-calcium exchanger(NCX). Increased calcium inside the myocyte leads to an increase in cardiac contractility. The most common cardiac manifestations of digitalis toxicity include atrioventricular junctionalrhythm, premature ventricular depolarizations, ventricular bigeminy, ventriculartachycardia, and second-degree AV blockade. Factors that increase the risk of digoxin toxicity are: • Hypercalcemia 1156 • Hypomagnesemia • Hypokalemia- It increases the binding of the digoxin to the Na+/K+ ATPase pump. • Drugs causing hypokalemia- loop and thiazide diuretics, amphotericin B, corticosteroids • Drugs that decrease digoxin elimination (inhibitors of P-glycoprotein) • Renal failure • Hypothyroidism Triamterene, atenolol, and potassium chloride cause hyperkalemia, and therefore do not causedigoxin toxicity.
subject: Pharmacology

question: What is the mechanism of action of methotrexate in osteosarcoma?
explanation: The anticancer activity of methotrexate is by inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR). Methotrexate belongs to the antimetabolite class of anticancer drugs. The antifolate action of thedrug is responsible for its anti-cancer properties. Mechanism of action: It is a folic acid analog and binds to the active catalytic site of dihydrofolate reductase(DHFR).This would inhibit the formation of tetrahydrofolate(THF) which is needed for purine nucleotides,thymidylate, and the amino acids serine and methionine. This would interfere with the productionof DNA, RNA, and important cellular proteins. Low doses of methotrexate are used in the management of rheumatic diseases. It is due to theinhibition of amino-imidazole carboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) transformylase andthymidylate synthetase. This results in increased levels of adenosine that inhibits inflammation. Adverse effects: 1157 Common side effects are nausea and mucosal ulcers. Others include anemia, leukopenia,stomatitis, GI ulcerations, and alopecia. Dose-related hepatotoxicity is also seen. The GI effectsand hepatotoxicity can be reduced by the use of leucovorin or folinic acid.
subject: Pharmacology

question: What should not be consumed by patients with bacterial vaginosis and trichomoniasis onmetronidazole?
explanation: Alcohol should not be consumed by a patient on metronidazole. Metronidazole producesa disulfiram-like reaction. If the patient consumes alcohol during or within 3 days of therapy, theymay experience abdominal distress, vomiting, headache, and flushing. Disulfiram and disulfiram-like reactions: Disulfiram inhibits the aldehyde dehydrogenase(ALDH) activity and thereby increases theconcentration of acetaldehyde in the blood. When a person treated with disulfiram consumesalcohol he or she would develop symptoms of acetaldehyde poisoning. The symptoms are: • Flushing • Pulsating headache • Nausea and vomiting • Sweating • Tachycardia • Hypotension • Orthostatic syncope • Vertigo • Blurred vision Certain drugs can also produce disulfiram-like reactions if alcohol is consumed along with thesedrugs. Patients should be warned not to use alcohol along with these drugs. The drugs include: • Metronidazole • Tinidazole • Cefoperazone • Sulfonylureas
subject: Pharmacology

question: A patient with chronic kidney disease underwent a nephrectomy. Which of the following canbe administered as a postoperative analgesic in this patient?
explanation: Acetaminophen can be given as an analgesic for the patient as it is the least nephrotoxic amongthe given options. Analgesia in CKD patients: Acetaminophen is considered a safer non-narcotic analgesic in chronic kidney disease (CKD)patients. For more severe pains opioid analgesics like tramadol or fentanyl are used. 1158 Even though acetaminophen is considered safe, with chronic high dosage it can also becomenephrotoxic. NSAIDs like naproxen, indomethacin, diclofenac, etc are not used in CKD patients because oftheir direct nephrotoxic effects. In healthy normal individuals, NSAIDs have little effect on renalfunction and blood pressure. But in conditions where the regulatory systems are impaired ashypovolemia, congestive heart failure, hepatic cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, or otherconditions where the renin-angiotensin system is activated, renal function by the formation ofprostaglandins are very important. NSAIDs cause impairment of prostaglandin-induced inhibition of chlorine reabsorption andantidiuretic hormone action. This will cause salt and water retention. It also inhibits COX-2derived prostaglandins which regulate the renal medullary blood flow and would lead to a rise inblood pressure, increased cardiovascular thrombotic events, and cardiac failure. It can also causeelectrolyte abnormalities like hyponatremia and hyperkalemia.
subject: Pharmacology

question: A patient with renal insufficiency presented with very low urine output, pedal edema,headache and BP 160/90. Which anti-hypertensive can be administered?
explanation: The antihypertensive that can be given in this case is chlorthalidone. The patient in this case ishaving renal insufficiency but there is no proteinuria mentioned in the question stem. So amongthe given options, the thiazide diuretic chlorthalidone can be administered as antihypertensive inthis patient. Management of hypertension in chronic kidney disease(CKD): ACE inhibitors or ARBs are considered the first-line drugs in patients with proteinuria. Theseagents effectively reduce blood pressure, proteinuria and prevent kidney decline. Calcium channelblockers can be added if necessary. For patients who do not have proteinuria, there is no established first-line therapy. One or two ofthe following drugs can be used: • Thiazides/thiazide-like diuretics • ACE inhibitors or ARBs • Calcium channel blockers In patients presenting with fluid retention or fluid overload, thiazide diuretics such aschlorthalidone and hydrochlorothiazide are recommended for management. In CKD stages 1 to 3(GFR >=30ml/min), thiazides are recommended, while loop diuretics such as bumetanide,furosemide are used in stages 4-5 (GFR < 30ml/min). Other options: Option A: Aliskiren is a direct renin inhibitor. It effectively lowers blood pressure, reducesalbuminuria, and limits left ventricular hypertrophy. Option C: Amlodipine is a calcium channel blocker. A common side effect of amlodipine is theproduction of peripheral edema. Option D: Prazosin is a selective α1 antagonist. It is generally not used as an initial agent to treathypertension, except in symptomatic prostatism or nightmares linked to posttraumatic stressdisorder. Headache is one of the side effects of prazosin. 1159
subject: Pharmacology

question: Which of the following interleukin (IL) is inhibited by tocilizumab?
explanation: Tocilizumab inhibits IL-6. Tocilizumab is a newer humanized antibody. It binds to the soluble, membrane-bound IL-6receptors and inhibits IL-6 mediated signaling. IL-6 can cause T-cell activation, acute-phaseprotein synthesis, and stimulation of inflammatory processes in diseases like rheumatoid arthritis. Uses: • Rheumatoid arthritis - It is a biological DMARD and is indicated in adult patients havingmoderate to severe disease with inadequate response to one or more DMARDs. • Juvenile idiopathic arthritis - It can be given for active systemic juvenile idiopathicarthritis(SJIA) or polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis(PJIA) in patients of 2 years of age ormore. Adverse effects: Common adverse effects include upper respiratory infections, hypertension, headache, andelevation of hepatic enzymes. It is also associated with serious infections including TB andopportunistic infections. Neutropenia and reduction in platelet count can also occur. Other options: Option B- IL-2 receptor inhibitors are daclizumab, basiliximab. They are used asimmunosuppressive agents following renal and heart transplants. Option C- IL-4 receptor inhibitor is dupilumab. They have been shown to reduce exacerbations inasthma. Option D- IL-5 inhibitors are mepolizumab, reslizumab, benralizumab. They have been shown toreduce exacerbations in asthma. 1160
subject: Pharmacology

question: The extent of drug absorption is represented by:
explanation: The extent of drug absorption is represented by the area under the curve. The rate and extent of absorption of a drug from dosage form administered by any route refer tothe bioavailability of a drug. Bioavailability is determined by the concentration-time curve inblood or by its excretion in urine. The area under the blood concentration-time curve (AUC) isproportional to the dose and the extent of bioavailability of a drug. Bioavailability is defined as the fraction of unchanged drug that reaches systemic circulation. Itcan be represented by the formula: Bioavailability(F) = Quantity of drug reaching systemic circulation/ Quantity of drug administered. Bioavailability depends on two factors: • Absorption • 1st pass metabolism The area under the plot of plasma concentration of a drug versus time after dosage is calledthe area under the curve or AUC. It can be used as a measure of the bioavailability of a drug andto calculate its clearance rate from the body. The image given below shows the AUC (bioavailability) in a plasma concentration-time curve: 1181 Bioavailability of drug injected intravenously is 100%, but it is lower after oral ingestion becauseof incomplete absorption and first-pass metabolism in the intestinal wall/liver. The image below shows the difference between the bioavailability of drugs injectedintravenously(iv) and orally(PO). Note the area under the respective curves is shaded in red andblue colours which represent the absorption of the drug.
subject: Pharmacology

question: Which of the following statement is correct regarding the given graph?

options.a: Drug 1 represents agonist and drug 2 represents inverse agonist
options.b: Drug 3 represents agonist and drug 4 represents inverse agonist
options.c: Drug 1 represents agonist and drug 4 represents inverse agonist
options.d: Drug 2 represents partial agonist and drug 3 represents inverse agonist

explanation: The correct statement is Drug 1 represents agonist and drug 4 represents inverse agonist. Graph 1 represents the agonist: An agonist is an agent which initiates the normal physiologicalresponse when combined with a receptor. Example: Salbutamol is a beta-2 receptor agonist. 1182 Graph 2 represents a partial agonist: An agent which produces a submaximal or partial effectwhen combined with a receptor. Example: Buprenorphine and butorphanol are partial agonists at opioid receptors. Graph 3 represents the antagonist: An agent which blocks or reduces the action of an agonist on areceptor, but does not have any effect of its own. Example: Naltrexone and naloxone are antagonists at opioid receptors Graph 4 represents an inverse agonist: An agent which activates a receptor to produce an effect inthe opposite direction to that of the agonist. Example: β-Carboline is an inverse agonist at benzodiazepine site of GABA-A receptor. The image given below shows action of various types of selective receptor modulators.
subject: Pharmacology

question: Which among the following drugs is the new FDA approved immune check point inhibitor forcarcinoma endometrium?
explanation: The new FDA-approved immune checkpoint inhibitor for carcinoma endometrium ispembrolizumab. Pembrolizumab acts by inhibiting programmed death receptor - 1 (PD-1) and was used for thetreatment of advanced melanoma. Now, the FDA has approved the use of pembrolizumab for anycancer with mismatch repair (MMR) deficiency or high microsatellite instability (MSI-H). On March 21, 2022, the food and drug administration approved pembrolizumab, as a single agent,for patients with advanced endometrial carcinoma that is microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H)or mismatch repair deficient (dMMR), as determined by an FDA-approved test. Other options: Option A: Nivolumab is an immune checkpoint inhibitor that acts by inhibiting programmeddeath receptor - 1 (PD-1) and is used for the treatment of advanced melanomaand relapsed/refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma. 1183 Option C: Trastuzumab is a monoclonal antibody that inhibits the HER2 receptor. It is used inthe treatment of HER2-positive breast cancer. Option D: Ipilimumab is a monoclonal antibody that binds to cytotoxic T lymphocyte–associatedProtein 4 (CTLA-4) and is approved for the treatment of late-stage melanoma.
subject: Pharmacology

question: Which of the following is not an immune checkpoint inhibitor?
explanation: Cetuximab is not an immune checkpoint inhibitor. Cetuximab is a monoclonal antibody againstepidermal growth factor receptor(EGFR). It is used for the treatment of colon cancer and headand neck squamous cell cancer. Other options. Option A: Nivolumab is an immune checkpoint inhibitor. It acts by inhibiting programmed deathreceptor - 1 (PD-1) and is used for the treatment of advanced melanoma and classical Hodgkinlymphoma. Option B: Pembrolizumab is an immune checkpoint inhibitor. It acts by inhibiting programmeddeath receptor - 1 (PD-1) and is used for the treatment of advanced melanoma. In 2021, approvalwas granted for the treatment of patients with endometrial carcinoma that progressed aftersystemic treatment, in combination with lenvatinib. Option C: Atezolimumab is an immune checkpoint inhibitor. It acts by inhibiting programmeddeath-ligand - 1 (PDL-1) and is used for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer. Important note: The FDA on May 2021 approved the use of nivolumab in patients having completely resectedesophageal or gastroesophageal junction cancers with residual pathologic disease who havereceived neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy.
subject: Pharmacology

question: NAPQI is the metabolite of which of the following drug toxicity?
explanation: N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine (NAPQI) is a metabolite of paracetamol drug toxicity. Paracetamol is an analgesic and antipyretic with weak anti-inflammatory action. It is mainlymetabolized in the liver by conjugation with glucuronic acid and sulfate and is excreted in theurine. At toxic doses, the glucuronide and sulfate conjugation pathway becomes saturated. Themetabolites of paracetamol get converted into NAPQI. NAPQI is highly reactive and causesenzymatic dysfunction in the liver. Normally, minor amounts of NAPQI produced in our body arerapidly eliminated by conjugation with reduced glutathione(GSH) and then excreted into theurine. Therefore, paracetamol toxicity is treated with N-acetyl cysteine(NAC), which replenishesGSH. NAC thereby helps in the excretion of NAPQI from the body. N-acetyl cysteine is ananti-oxidant and functions by detoxifying NAPQI. Paracetamol poisoning is the most common cause of liver failure necessitating transplantation. 1184 The maximum dose of acetaminophen that can be given is 4 g/day.
subject: Pharmacology

question: Identify the correct match, regarding the drug and its adverse effect.
explanation: The correct match is verapamil causes constipation. Verapamil is a calcium channel blocker used for the treatment of paroxysmal supraventriculartachycardia, atrial fibrillation, and atrial flutter. Bradycardia and constipation are the importantside effects of verapamil. Other options: Option A: Hydralazine is a vasodilator used in the treatment of heart failure, and hypertensiveemergencies, especially preeclampsia. The drug is used as a combination pill containingisosorbide dinitrate (BiDil) in the treatment of heart failure. The important side effect ofhydralazine is drug-induced lupus. Option B: Atenolol is a cardioselective beta-1 blocker used in the treatment of angina andhypertension. Atenolol doesn't cause hemolytic anemia. Option C: Aliskiren is a direct renin inhibitor used as an alternative antihypertensive drug forthose who do not respond or do not tolerate 1st line drugs. The side effect of aliskiren ishyperkalemia and not hypokalemia.
subject: Pharmacology

question: A lady who had undergone mastectomy for breast cancer is being treated with tamoxifen.How long should it be stopped for before she can conceive?

options.d: Can be stopped and conceived soon after stopping

explanation: In a post-mastectomy patient undergoing therapy with tamoxifen, it should be stopped for 3months before she can conceive. Tamoxifen is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) and is used as a chemotherapeuticagent in receptor positive breast cancer patients to prevent recurrence after surgery. It is the drugof choice in pre-menopausal women. It has an agonistic action on the endometrium, leading toan increased risk of endometrial cancers (2 fold risk). Hence, it is not used in post-menopausalwomen. It is contraindicated in pregnancy due to teratogenic effects such as craniofacial abnormalities andreproductive tract abnormalities. For the same reason, it has to be stopped for 3 months (due tolong half-life) prior to conceiving. It is also stopped during lactation as it is secreted in breastmilk. Other complications of tamoxifen include deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, andhot flashes. Other breast cancer risk reduction techniques: • Lifestyle modification: Low-calorie diet, daily exercise, no smoking, no drinking, etc. • More frequent screening with mammogram +/- MRI • Chemoprevention: Preferred in women >35 years of age in patients who are ER/PR positive.Given for 5-10 years. 1185 • SERMS (selective estrogen receptor modulators) - Tamoxifen and raloxifene. These have adverseeffects. • Aromatase Inhibitors (AIs): They are used only in post-menopausal women. • Risk-reduction surgeries: preferred in patients with BRCA1/2 mutations or patients withfirst-degree relatives with breast cancers. Provides >90% risk-reduction. preferred in patientswho have completed their family. • Bilateral mastectomy • Salpingo-oophorectomy: Best results when done < 40 years of age.
subject: Pharmacology

question: A young boy with a history of multiple blood transfusions presents with bone pain for thepast 6 months. A peripheral smear showed sickle-shaped RBCs. Which of the following drugsare not used in the treatment of his condition?
explanation: Bebtelovimab is not used in the treatment of sickle cell disease. The clinical features of multipleblood transfusions, bone pain, and sickle cells on peripheral smear are suggestive of sickle celldisease. Bebtelovimab is the new monoclonal antibody used for the treatment of COVID-19. It works bybinding to the spike protein of the COVID-19 virus. It has been found useful in reducing the riskof hospitalization or death. Bebtelovimab retains the activity against the omicron variant. Other options: Option B: Voxelotor is an inhibitor of hemoglobin S polymerase and stabilizer of sickle cellhemoglobin (HbS) that is used in the therapy of sickle cell disease. Option C: Hydroxyurea improves fetal haemoglobin (HbF) and is the primary drug for controllingHbS in sickle cell disease. Thus improving the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood. Hydroxyureaalso inhibits the enzyme ribonucleotide reductase (RNR), which is a rate-limiting step in thebiosynthesis of DNA. This property of hydroxyurea is used in the treatment of various cancers,and myeloproliferative disorders like chronic myelogenous leukemia, and polycythemia. Option D: L-glutamine is a naturally occurring amino acid with antioxidant properties.It increases the availability of reduced glutathione which may lessen oxidative damage in sicklered blood cells.
subject: Pharmacology

question: The half-life of letrozole is:
explanation: The half-life of letrozole is 45 hours. Letrozole is a reversible aromatase inhibitor. It is a non-steroidal compound that inhibits thearomatization of estrogen thereby causing estrogen depletion. Letrozole is rapidly absorbed with99.9% oral bioavailability and has a t½ of around 41 hours. Letrozole is used as the first-line drug for estrogen-positive breast cancer following mastectomy inpost-menopausal women. Adverse effects of letrozole are due to the depletion of estrogen. The commonly seen adverseeffects are hot flashes, vaginal dryness, nausea, diarrhea, dyspepsia, accelerated bone loss, and 1186 thinning of hair.
subject: Pharmacology

question: Identify the false statement about eicosanoids.
explanation: A false statement about eicosanoids is they are synthesized from arginine. Eicosanoids aresynthesized from arachidonic acid (Option B) Eicosanoids are the most universally distributed autocoids in the body. Prostaglandins,thromboxanes, and leukotrienes comprise eicosanoids. Every cell is capable of synthesizing one ormore eicosanoids. Platelets primarily synthesize thromboxanes (Option D). Eicosanoids are synthesized from arachidonic acid. Arachidonic acid is derived from membranephospholipids. The release of arachidonic acid (AA) from the membrane phospholipids is mainlymediated by phospholipase A. AA is metabolized by cyclooxygenases to produce prostaglandins and lipoxygenases to produceleukotrienes and lipoxins. Inhibitors of metabolism of arachidonic acid: • Corticosteroids cause inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis by inhibiting phospholipase A2. • Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory (NSAIDs) drugs inhibit the synthesis of prostaglandins byinhibiting the enzyme cyclooxygenase. • Zileuton inhibits the enzyme lipoxygenase thereby decreasing the synthesis of leukotrienes. Chemically, all prostaglandins are considered to be derivatives of prostanoic acid, having afive-carbon ring (Option C). The image given below shows the synthesis of various eicosanoids from arachidonic acid:
